cases.rationale: Install and exact app/runtime queries, runnable A then B, successful uninstall, failed app query, and empty app-only enumeration with the runtime still queryable. No general selection, noninteractive, or remote-property credit.
Transactions followed by exact public installed-ref/commit queries; uninstall followed by the public NOT_INSTALLED error. CLI launches supply state evidence but do not cover library launch APIs.
A denied payload request and failed update precede exact unchanged app/runtime commits and runnable A. No exact download-error or whole-transaction rollback claim.
Public transaction failure after injected payload error, followed by exact unchanged installed refs. Logged signals and operation getters are not asserted.
Successful update with the remote still advertising A; exact app/runtime commit queries and runnable A before and after.
Successful public update transaction with unchanged exact commits. No claim that a skipped operation emits operation-done.
Repeat install while B is available, require success and an already-installed warning, then verify exact A/runtime commits and runnable A.
After positive install assertions, repeat install while B is available; require the public ALREADY_INSTALLED domain/code and unchanged exact installed refs.
Require a missing-ref error identifying the requested app and successful empty enumeration of all installed refs. No sandbox, populated enumeration, or formatting coverage.
Require public REF_NOT_FOUND and non-NULL empty installed-ref enumeration. An empty result does not exercise the client's per-element formatting loop.
Missing query and uninstall diagnostics identify the absent ref; after each, exact existing app/runtime commits and runnable A are checked.
Missing query and uninstall require public NOT_INSTALLED; after each, existing app/runtime commits are checked through public queries.
Fail a payload request and verify preserved A/runtime; restore downloads, require another payload request and successful update, then exact B/runtime commits and runnable B.
Public transaction failure preserves A/runtime, followed by a new successful transaction, a restored payload request and exact B/runtime installed commits.

Separate CLI processes read back exact remote name/URL/title/priority columns after creation and edits; priority changes reverse order; deletion removes one remote and preserves the other. Equal-priority CLI order is not promised or asserted.

Fresh client processes enumerate and look up exact remote properties after public add/modify/remove calls. Priority changes reverse order, setting title NULL is observed as NULL, and deleted-remote lookup fails while another remote survives. Tied priority order and unasserted remote-ref metadata get no credit.

Freshly added reverse-alphabetical names with equal priorities must retain insertion order, ahead of a lower-priority remote. Kept separate because reference Flatpak 1.19.1 disagrees with its public documentation; a failing result earns no verified credit.

Require the public ready callback to run, return FALSE, prevent new-operation events, fail the transaction and leave no installed refs. A new transaction returning TRUE installs exact app/runtime commits. Other logged signals get no coverage credit.
